deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a short printed-form business note (letterhead form 'Herrn ... zur Nachricht', with 'zur Nachricht' struck through) from the Braunschweig bookseller G. C. E. Meyer sen. to 'Herrn Professor Dr. ph. Dedekind, Hochwohlgeboren', dated Braunschweig, 20/6 76 (20 June 1876).

Translation: 'Immediately on receipt of your esteemed order, I ordered Zolotareff, Théorie des nombres [entiers complexes] by direct post from Petersburg. As the work has not yet arrived, I have today written once more to the publisher and now expect its earliest arrival. Most obediently, G. C. E. Meyer sen.'

The previous folio appears to be the St. Petersburg side of the same transaction. It is a note from the imperial court bookseller Carl Röttger (branch: H. Schmitzdorff, St. Petersburg) addressed to Meyer in Braunschweig, concerning the same Zolotareff title.

The work in question is almost certainly E. I. Zolotarev, 'Théorie des nombres entiers complexes, avec une application au calcul intégral' (St. Petersburg, 1874). In it Zolotarev developed his own theory of factorization in algebraic number fields, a parallel route to Dedekind's ideals and Kronecker's divisors.

The historical point of the page is this: by June 1876 Dedekind had placed an order for Zolotarev's book and was still waiting for it. This was during the period when he was revising his ideal theory: the 1876–77 French exposition in the Bulletin des sciences mathématiques, and the 1879 third edition of Dirichlet's Vorlesungen, Supplement XI.

There are no derivations to reconstruct.

results.what: Documentary evidence that Dedekind ordered Zolotarev's 'Théorie des nombres entiers complexes' (1874) through a Braunschweig bookseller, with the book not yet received by 20 June 1876.
results.modern_name: Bibliographic and correspondence evidence about Dedekind's reading of Zolotarev's theory of algebraic integers and ideals
results.usually_credited_to: N/A (historical fact). Dedekind's awareness of Zolotarev is mentioned in the literature on the history of ideal theory, e.g. in work on Zolotarev's theory and its comparison with Dedekind and Kronecker.

deep.surprise_reason: Purely a bookseller's letter with no mathematical content. It gives a minor datable detail (June 1876) on when Dedekind sought Zolotarev's ideal-theoretic work, which is of mild interest to historians of algebraic number theory but not surprising.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription is essentially correct. The date reads '20/6 76', i.e. 20 June 1876.
The struck-out word before 'Ankommen' is uncertain; 'Eintreffen' is plausible but not clearly legible.
On the previous page, 'J. C. Meyer' is presumably the same bookseller 'G. C. E. Meyer' of Braunschweig.
The title should be understood as Zolotareff, 'Théorie des nombres [entiers complexes]'; the letter abbreviates it to 'théorie des nombres'.
